COVID: Virtual life - The Future is Now

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With billions around the world confined to their homes thanks to Covid-19, we have become ever more reliant on social media for communication, accelerating trend forecasters predictions of our future.

Unique Selling Point:
Covid-19 has changed the world as we know it. In this new era of social distancing, we have become even more reliant on the internet for communication. Tonight on Carte Blanche we showcase a range of technologies that have allowed us to virtually interact with one another, helping us to navigate a post-covid-19 world, bringing us closer whilst staying apart.

Summary:
Futurists and Trend Analysts were asked to predict what the world would like in 5-10 years time. They imagined a more decentralized world underpinned by technology in which we work from home instead of the office, enjoy musical concerts on social media platforms, visit virtual art galleries, consult with Doctors online and experience conferences from the comfort of our sofas aided by virtual and augmented reality.

But now Covid-19 has turned the world upside down and accelerated those forecasts. With billions around the world under lockdown, we have literally become generation Z for zoomers overnight- because that's the way we have meetings now. You might pinch yourself because future is well and truly now!

Press Release:


Just a few years ago, futurists and trend analysts were predicting what the world would look like in five to ten years’ time. They imagined a more decentralised world underpinned by technology in which working from home instead of the office would be the new normal, music concerts would happen on social media platforms and visiting virtual art galleries and consulting with doctors online would become standard. Now COVID-19 has turned the world upside down and accelerated that future right into the present.

Script:


OPENING LINK: A revolution is taking place right before our eyes and we’re able to experience the birth of a brave new world from the comfort of our living rooms.

Lockdown is forcing us to connect to the world in new and innovative ways and I for one am so excited about the possibilities.

It’s a future that was predicted by trend analysts like Dion Chang but because of COVID-19, that future is happening now.


Dion Chang on how the future he predicted is happening now


V/O: In this new reality, millions around the world now work from home. It’s something that big corporations have been planning for. One example is MTN as Jacqui O’Sullivan explains.

Jacqui on MTN planning for lockdown
Many departments are able to work from home, including call centres.

V/O: Marketing Expert Mark Schaeffer believes COVID-19 will force companies to adopt new technologies faster

Mark on businesses adapting to COVID-19

V/O: If you want to see what true human connection looks like in a post-Covid world, look no further than the Eventing Industry.

With public gatherings banned for the foreseeable future, event producers like Philippa Hudson Bennet are turning to virtual reality technologies to survive.

Philippa intros VR in the eventing industry.

On producing an virtual awards ceremony in June

Demoing VR to Claire

V/O: Another innovator in the VR space is Rick Treweek who recently attended a Virtual Conference.

Rick on attending a virtual VR Conference

Demoing the virtual space to Claire


V/O: But it’s not just work that’s being done at home. There’s a lot of play happening too

LINK TO MUSIC: (Watching the one-world concert)

The Lady Gaga-curated One World Together at Home concert was watched by almost 21 million people a few weeks back. And locally, DJ Shimza’s online gigs are attracting audiences of close on a million people.

DJ Shimza on the Lockdown parties

V/O: Local singer-songwriters like Louise Carver are also using social media platforms to perform regularly to their fans.

Louise Carver on her Sunday Lounge Sessions

V/O: As we enter the 5th month of the pandemic, there are fears for the entire academic year. That’s why tertiary institutions have ramped up their online programmes.

WITS University began their new semester last week entirely online according to vice chancellor Adam Habib

Adam Habib on the WITS Online programme

On trying to make it available to all – supplying laptops to those who don’t have them

On Zero rating data partnerships with mobile networks – soundbyte from Jacqui O’Sullivan

Comment from Dion Chang about virtual tuition and Adam saying the future will be a hybrid of the two.

V/O: Another innovation allows for people to consult with doctors from the comfort of their living rooms

Virtual Doctor Consult

V/O: But can all real world experiences be recreated virtually? When it comes to Church services, Pastor Dewald De Kock says emphatically yes!

Dewald on virtual church services

V/O: Amidst the fear and uncertainty being caused by the pandemic, there is still great optimism and hope for the future. So what does a post-COVID-19 world look like?

Closing comments from Dion & Mark
